title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Just Delivered Great News to Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Before Nov. 25?
detail:
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Just Delivered Great News to Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Before Nov. 25?
Bram Berkowitz, The Motley Fool

Things certainly change fast in today's news cycle.

Last week, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent appeared on Fox News and delivered what seemed to be a blistering rebuke of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), which is facing allegations of potentially violating export controls.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Furthermore, Bessent called for a "dramatic shake-up" at Nvidia, suggesting that the artificial intelligence chip giant's next leader should be from "outside the company."

But now Bessent seems to have left the door open for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to return as CEO. It's certainly good news for Huang. Should you buy Nvidia stock before Nov. 25?

Image source: The White House.

Bessent appears to change tune

Looking back at the Fox interview, I interpreted that to mean Bessent and his colleagues at the Treasury Department were not interested in seeing Huang return as Nvidia's CEO. But Bessent appears to have changed his tune, or was simply misunderstood.

On CBS' Face the Nation on Nov. 22, when pressed whether Nvidia should look for an outside candidate to lead Nvidia, Bessent replied, "I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now," seemingly leaving the door open for Huang to return as Nvidia's CEO.

As of this writing, the odds of Huang returning as Nvidia's CEO on the prediction-markets platform Kalshi have increased from 7% on Nov. 20 to 12%.

The new sentiment may be tied to recent comments from President Donald Trump, who has come out in support of Huang and called on Nvidia's board of directors to reinstate the man who co-founded the company over three decades ago.

Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12, following allegations of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who may have been a Chinese spy. The alleged woman, Alice Huang (no relation), has also been accused of setting up a network to illegally divert Nvidia chips to Chinese companies, despite export restrictions.

Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation into the matter, and regulators have probed the company at the center of the allegations, a Singaporean data center company called MegaSpeed. Huang is also set to testify before Congress.

Last week, Bessent also said that Nvidia must inform the Trump administration by Nov. 25 whether it set up shell companies to evade export controls and sell its most advanced chips to Chinese firms. In his interview on Nov. 22, Bessent said the Treasury Department had not yet received those answers.

title: Jeff Bezos sends a strong signal to Nvidia stock investors as CEO search heats up

Jeff Bezos sends a strong signal to Nvidia stock investors as CEO search heats up
Jean Christine, Aparajita Chatterjee
Sun, November 22, 2026 at 2:07 PM MST 5 min read
NVDA
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Nvidia has had exactly one CEO since 1993. Now it needs a second, and plenty of famous names in tech have opinions about who should get the job.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is one of them. His advice matters to anyone whose 401(k) or index fund holds Nvidia stock, because he thinks the chipmaker's board should look inside the building before it looks anywhere else.

Bezos would keep the job in the family

"If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider," Bezos said at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World conference on Nov. 17. "Nvidia is too complicated."

He doesn't think much of a newcomer's odds.

"I think outside CEOs in complex companies have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding," Bezos said. "And so I would always think that's a last resort."

More Bezos: Jeff Bezos says 2 policies drive up housing costs, and it's 'not hard to figure out'

Bezos followed that advice himself at Amazon. He handed the CEO job to Andy Jassy, the longtime head of Amazon Web Services, in July 2021. Bezos called his exit a "multi-year planned transition," which is nothing like what Nvidia just went through.

Bezos stayed out of whether Huang should get his job back, saying he didn't know enough about what happened behind closed doors. He did have praise for Huang.

"Jensen is a remarkable guy who founded and built a remarkable company with a lot of hard work and foresight," Bezos said. "And he deserves admiration and respect no matter what, and that will never go away."

Jeff Bezos says hiring an outside CEO should be Nvidia's "last resort."Chesnot / Getty Images
Huang raised his hand and the board said no

Nvidia announced on Nov. 12 that Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member, according to the company's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. He left after admitting to an extramarital affair. Chief financial officer Colette Kress stepped in as interim CEO, and longtime director Harvey Jones became the board's first-ever chair.

Read more:

Jeff Bezos says your family is 'not going to need' 2 paychecks thanks to AI

Warren Buffett told Jeff Bezos the real reason people don't just 'copy' his investing strategy to get rich

Jensen Huang was 'broken and shattered' in final hours as Nvidia CEO

On the same day Bezos spoke, Huang said he wanted back in.

"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang wrote in a post on X Nov. 17. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

Micah Zimmerman, The Motley Fool

The most interesting thing Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG) made this year might be a diaper.

It's called Pampers Amoira, P&G's most premium diaper yet. It was built on a simple insight: Families are having fewer babies, so parents are willing to spend more on each one. CFO Andre Schulten said Amoira is on track to top $100 million in U.S. sales in its first year.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

That one product says a lot about where P&G is headed, and it's why I'd want to own the stock before 2027. The 70-year dividend streak is just the bonus.

A new boss with a new playbook

Jejurikar, a P&G lifer who joined in 1989, became CEO on Jan. 1. He isn't tearing up the strategy so much as changing how it's carried out. P&G is spending more time in shoppers' homes, making brand content for algorithm-driven social feeds, and working with retailers on everything from store displays to AI shopping tools.

It's working so far. Organic sales rose 4% last quarter, mostly because people bought more products rather than paid higher prices. "Growth going forward is not about taking share. Growth going forward is about growing our categories," Schulten said.

P&G also bought Thorne, a premium supplements brand. "It's a really well-run operation, and it's been around for a long time," Jejurikar told CNBC.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Why 2027 should look better

The biggest reason is a restructuring program that cuts up to 7,000 non-manufacturing jobs and exits some weaker brands and markets over two fiscal years. Schulten called it "an important step toward ensuring our ability to deliver our long-term algorithm over the coming two to three years." In this year's annual report letter, Jejurikar wrote that P&G is "committed to improving results semester by semester and year by year."

The road there runs through higher oil prices, though. "Due to the duration of higher oil prices, we now expect materially higher cost headwinds in Q2 and the second half of fiscal 2027," Schulten warned, and P&G is "closely watching consumer demand as high fuel and energy costs persist into the fall and winter." That's partly why P&G expects core earnings growth of just 0% to 3% this fiscal year, and its pricing power is limited, since price increases had only a minor effect on sales last quarter.

title: Your 401(k) Has New Contribution Limits for 2027. Here's What You Need to Know
detail:
Your 401(k) Has New Contribution Limits for 2027. Here's What You Need to Know
Stefon Walters, The Motley Fool
Sun, November 22, 2026 at 12:50 PM MST 4 min read
NVDA
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

At this point, 401(k)s have become synonymous with retirement accounts because so many Americans have one. It's by far the most used retirement account in the U.S., and it's why millions can have a financially comfortable retirement.

A 401(k) is a true win-win. It helps you save and invest for retirement proactively, and you get a tax break for doing so. There are many moving parts to a 401(k), but one key rule to keep track of is the contribution limit. Let's dive into what to expect next year.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Changes to the 401(k) contribution limit

Beginning next year, you can contribute $25,500 to a 401(k), up from this year's $24,500 limit. If you're 50 or older, you can add an $8,500 catch-up contribution (up from $8,000), bringing your limit to $34,000.

Image source: Getty Images.

Workers aged 60 to 63 can make a special catch-up contribution of up to $11,750, meaning anyone in that four-year age range can contribute $37,250 to their 401(k)s in 2027. Once you turn 64 or older, you go back to the standard catch-up amount.

The contribution limit applies only to your personal contributions. If your job matches a certain amount of your contributions, that match doesn't count against your limit. For example, if you're younger than 50 and your job matches up to $15,000 annually, you can also contribute $15,000, even though $30,000 is above the $25,500 limit for 2027.

Not many people can afford to max out their 401(k)s year in and year out, but you should try to contribute at least the amount your employer will match. It's essentially "free" money because it's a guaranteed instant 100% return on your investment. Don't leave it on the table.

How IRA limits changed

IRA contribution limits often increase, but they're staying put next year. The contribution limit for IRAs -- both traditional and Roth combined -- is $7,500. People 50 or older can add a $1,100 catch-up contribution, bringing the limit to $8,600.

A couple of changes, however, are the income limits for contributing to a Roth IRA or claiming a traditional IRA deduction. Below are the new income limits to be eligible to contribute to a Roth IRA:

One of the most fascinating parts of Berkshire Hathaway's sprawling business is its roughly $360 billion equity portfolio, in which the company invests the float generated by its insurance business in a wide range of stocks across sectors.

In his more than six decades as CEO of Berkshire, Warren Buffett built one of the best investing track records in history. He has since passed the torch to new CEO Greg Abel, a longtime Berkshire veteran and close confidant of Buffett, who plans to continue Buffett's remarkably concentrated approach to investing.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

To this day, just three stocks make up nearly 47% of Berkshire's portfolio. Perhaps even more amazing is that none of these three are traditional artificial intelligence hyperscalers.

While Berkshire's investment moves are a strong starting point, investors should realize that Berkshire rarely explains its positions. Its filings arrive with a delay, so treat them as a starting point for your own research, not a shopping list.

Greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images.

Apple -- 22.3%

Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) is Berkshire's largest position by a wide margin. The roughly 228 million shares haven't changed in four straight quarterly filings, a notable pause after Buffett trimmed the stake for nearly two years.

Buffett, Abel, and the Berkshire team probably like Apple due to its loyal customer base of more than 2.5 billion active devices, high-margin Services revenue, and massive share repurchases over the past decade-plus that have significantly reduced Apple's outstanding shares, thereby increasing Berkshire's slice of profits.

Apple repurchased $24 billion of stock in its latest quarter, on top of a new $100 billion authorization announced in the spring.

With a market capitalization above $5 trillion, Apple is now the largest stock in the world by market value. The results back it up: Fiscal 2026 revenue hit a record $478.8 billion, up 15%, and earnings per share rose 20% to $8.98. September-quarter iPhone revenue set a record, and services revenue also reached an all-time high of $31.6 billion.

Trading around 39 times trailing earnings, Apple stock isn't cheap. It has a new CEO, John Ternus, and shareholders are keen to ensure the company can keep producing innovative consumer tech products.

Anthropic's (NASDAQ:ANT) IPO was a smashing success. It broke the 5-month-old record for the biggest IPO ever and opened well above its IPO price. Clearly, many investors and analysts are excited about the company's prospects, and that is already being reflected in various price targets. For instance, Scott Berg, an analyst at Needham & Company, initiated coverage of the stock with a $150 price target. That implies an almost 72% upside from current levels. Could Anthropic really rise that much over the next year?

Image source: Anthropic.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

What a $150 stock price implies

At a stock price of $150, Anthropic's market cap would be about $2 trillion (it would be higher on a fully diluted basis). That would put the tech company in a very exclusive group. Here is an argument as to why this valuation could make sense, especially in 12 months, once we have more data on Anthropic's performance.

First, the company's revenue has been growing at a dizzying pace. Third-quarter revenue was $17 billion, up 1,127% year over year. Anthropic's run rate revenue grew by $10 billion in a single month, to $81 billion as of the end of October.

True, the company remains unprofitable. In the third quarter, its net loss was $23.3 billion, significantly worse than the $12.1 billion loss recorded in the prior-year quarter. But that was mostly due to non-cash charges driven by an increase in the value of various financial instruments -- a mostly paper loss that tells us very little about the fundamentals of Anthropic's business.

Meanwhile, several factors could allow the company's growth to maintain a strong pace. Anthropic arguably benefits from a competitive edge. For instance, with about 40 million users across its portfolio of AI-powered tools, including more than 1,900 customers with trailing 12-month revenue exceeding $1 million, Anthropic is building network effects.

Data and customer feedback can help the company improve its AI-powered tools and attract even more users. The company also argues that more sophisticated versions of its Claude frontier model will help it build even better ones next time around, strengthening its lead. Claude has been writing increasingly more code per person within the company.

Embedding this AI tool into Anthropic's workflows could lead to significant productivity gains in the medium term and allow the company to reduce expenses and turn a profit. Based on the company's run rate revenue and the pace at which it is growing, it could reach sales well above $100 billion in fiscal year 2027.

title: When Can Anthropic Insiders Sell? What the Post-IPO Lockup Period Means for Shareholders.
detail:
When Can Anthropic Insiders Sell? What the Post-IPO Lockup Period Means for Shareholders.
Jack Delaney, The Motley Fool
Sun, November 22, 2026 at 1:29 PM MST 4 min read

NVDA
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

After nearly every initial public offering (IPO), insiders and pre-IPO stakeholders have to wait for a period before they can sell shares on the open market. These lockup periods can last for up to a year, but their expirations always cause some concern among new shareholders. After all, if insiders flood the market with their shares and demand from buyers doesn't keep up with supply, it can put downward pressure on the stock price.

For Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT), which went public on Nov. 19, employees and executives will eventually have the opportunity to sell more of their shares. But instead of lockup periods ending, there are higher priorities for shareholders to focus on.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The selling time frame

If employees start selling when a lockup period ends, that shouldn't be viewed as an automatic red flag or a signal that they have lost faith in their company. Rather, it's one of the first times they can turn the paper wealth they've accumulated over the years into actual liquid wealth.

For Anthropic, the lockup expirations are more staggered than a traditional IPO, with shares unlocking at several intervals over the next year — including one that took place Friday unlocking up to 315 million shares, and several more large events over the next couple of months. That just means that, instead of one selling date to focus on, there will be multiple selling points. That's important to note for anyone planning to invest in Anthropic, as they may see some choppy price action around those dates.

That said, lockup-related volatility is typically a short-term factor. The bigger drivers of the stock price over the long term will be revenue growth, spending, and profitability.

What will move the Anthropic stock price?

Anthropic is showing explosive top-line growth.

Revenue jumped roughly 1,200% in the first nine months of 2026 to $33.2 billion, and it now has approximately 250 customers spending $10 million or more on a 12-month trailing basis. In addition, its net revenue retention rate of approximately 900% as of Sept. 30 shows that existing customers are dramatically increasing their spending with Anthropic over time. These types of numbers support the case of a rapidly expanding business that can become more valuable.
